title: Neighbouring Erdos problems (#243, #251, #269, #1049) and the problem-owned library root

concepts.label: product-cleared reciprocal tail states (C, D)
concepts.description: Integer states with D(n+1) = a(n) D(n) and C(n+1) = a(n) C(n) - D(n); the denominator-cleared coordinates of a reciprocal tail sum 1/a(n) (nextDenState/nextTailState, ReciprocalTailRigidity.lean:35,39).

concepts.label: centered error E = D - (a-1) C
concepts.description: The signed defect whose vanishing is exactly the Sylvester step; the tail update is C(n+1) = C(n) - E(n) (centeredState, ReciprocalTailRigidity.lean:43).

concepts.label: Sylvester successor a -> a^2 - a + 1
concepts.description: The rigid recurrence that the #243 conclusion asserts must eventually hold; E(n) = 0 at every index is the same condition (sylvesterNext, ReciprocalTailRigidity.lean:31).

concepts.label: negative-state magnitude e = -E > 0
concepts.description: The live obstruction shape: a positive magnitude satisfying D(n) + e(n) = (a(n)-1) C(n), so that the tail state rises instead of descending.

concepts.label: tail gcd g(n) = gcd(C(n), D(n)) as a divisibility chain
concepts.description: A divisibility chain along the orbit: the gcd of the product-cleared tail and denominator states divides its successor, and at a negative-state index it equals gcd(C(n), e(n)) (tailGcd_dvd_succ, tailGcd_eq_gcd_negativeMagnitude, ReciprocalTailRigidity.lean:1086,1101).

concepts.label: shifted CRT block of pairwise-coprime moduli
concepts.description: Consecutive integers x, x+1, ..., x+B-1 each divisible by a prescribed fresh modulus, placed beyond any height; the arithmetic obstruction consumed by the bounded-rise no-go (exists_shifted_consecutiveMultiples, ReciprocalTailRigidity.lean:827).

concepts.label: division-free normalized vanishing: for every K eventually K*|E(n)| < C(n)
concepts.description: The zone's dominant unproved analytic input. Throughout this zone, hypotheses that merely fix the exact recurrence system (positivity, strict centering, the shape equation) are treated as regime declarations, whereas substantive unproved inputs of this kind are recorded as open antecedents.

concepts.label: survival through h forced divisions modulo (h+1)!
concepts.description: A finite-state reduction for the forced update ((n+1)a^2 - (n+2)a + (n+3)) / (n+2) (ForcedSurvives, FiniteHorizonResidue.lean:75).

concepts.label: dyadic prime series and its gap reindexing
concepts.description: Finite rational partial sums of p(i)/2^i and of the consecutive prime gaps; the objects of the #251 module (prime0DisplayedPartialSumQ, primeGapPartialSumQ, PrimeGapDyadicTail.lean:50,105).

concepts.label: abstract dyadic tail recurrence T(N+1) = 2 T(N) - g(N+1)
concepts.description: A hypothesised rational tail orbit with integer digits; never instantiated at the actual prime-gap series anywhere in the zone (DyadicTailRecurrence, PrimeGapDyadicTail.lean:123).

concepts.label: free integer carry K and its emitted coefficients 2K(n) - K(n+1)
concepts.description: The coboundary that produces any prescribed rational dyadic value from an arbitrary, non-periodic coefficient stream (carryCoeff, PrimeGapDyadicTail.lean:270).

concepts.label: running LCM height p^log_p x * q^log_q x * r^log_r x
concepts.description: The computational height attached to the {p,q,r}-smooth prefix below x, and the reciprocal kernel 1/height (threePrimeHeight, threePrimeKernelQ, ThreePrimeRunningLcm.lean:36,40).

concepts.label: logarithmic cells and pure-power jump set
concepts.description: The height is constant on cells where no log coordinate moves, and changes only at the 3*count+1 pure prime powers (SameThreePrimeLogCell, threePrimeJumpSetWithOrigin, ThreePrimeRunningLcm.lean:163,273).

concepts.label: smooth exponent shell in a short multiplicative interval
concepts.description: Exponent triples whose smooth value lies in [lo, hi) with hi <= base*lo; one coordinate is then pinned, giving a quadratic multiplicity bound (smoothExponentShell, ThreePrimeRunningLcm.lean:500).

concepts.label: residue escaping a polynomial tail window
concepts.description: bound < residue <= C; the terminal finite contradiction of the #269 residue-escape strategy, whose producer is absent (ResidueEscapesWindow, ResidueEscape.lean:17).

concepts.label: coordinatewise rational-base corridor
concepts.description: The finite package a^K | Q*digit, digit <= N+K, Q b^(N+K+1) < a^(K+1): a literal transfer of the integer-base Erdos corridor to base a/b (CoordinatewiseCorridor, RationalBaseLambert.lean:41).

concepts.label: cleared tail B r^N (F - prefix) with denominator-base tax s^(N+1)
concepts.description: The rational-base analogue of the integer-base cleared tail; the forcing term carries the extra factor s^(N+1) that is absent when s = 1 (rationalBaseClearedTailQ, RationalBaseLambert.lean:109).

concepts.label: doubled denominator exponents of the rational Pade construction
concepts.description: Twice the proposed common exponent (3n^2-n)/2 and the doubled P- and Q-summand exponents; pure polynomial bookkeeping with no analytic content (RationalPadeArithmetic.lean:18).

concepts.label: no real number, infinite series or Irrational statement anywhere in Z17
concepts.description: Grep over all nine modules finds no occurrence of a real-valued sum, tsum, or Irrational: every declaration is finite or abstract algebra, so no module reaches the actual value of #243, #251, #269 or #1049.

concepts.label: phase-specific density obstruction for the two cubic survivors
concepts.description: For Q_{12,1} and Q_{12,-1}, the tail recurrences force a mismatch in phase 0 or 1 modulo 7 respectively; the disjoint phase windows give lower density at least 1/7.

concepts.label: exact finite-window modulus pinning
concepts.description: The actual window product, rather than its dyadic lower bound, controls how a small residue pins a scaled normalized state near an integer.

concepts.label: conditional o(8^a) window equivalence
concepts.description: Exact window growth permits a conditional equivalence at scale 8^a when the selected cap is dominated and little-o for each positive denominator.

concepts.label: altered rational completion of a finite radix prefix
concepts.description: A finite positive radix/digit prefix can be preserved while the future is changed to a rationally completed orbit, blocking finite-prefix-only inference.

concepts.label: size-authenticated bounded certificate safety
concepts.description: Array-size hypotheses and sound Boolean predicates separate checked bounded data from default values and from cofinal conclusions.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: In the product-cleared reciprocal-tail system the next tail state is exactly the current one minus the centered error, C(n+1) = C(n) - E(n); and the whole system (denominator update, tail update, centered error) is equivariant under multiplying C and D by a common scale.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: One-line ring identities; the scale equivariance only removes duplicate search parameters.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: There is no infinite orbit of naturals with a(n) >= 2, D(n+1) = a(n) D(n) and a constant negative centered error, i.e. with D(n) + m = (a(n) - 1) (c + n m) for a fixed positive magnitude m and any initial tail state c; the same holds from any starting index onward. No growth condition on a is assumed.
statement_nodes.engine: prime-divisor pigeonhole: every multiplier must share a prime with m, and each such prime can occur in at most one multiplier
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Unassessed against the classical Erdos/Sylvester rigidity literature for sum 1/a(n) with a(n+1) >= a(n)^2. The statement is about the exact integer system only; the reciprocal series itself is never formed in this zone.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Excludes only the exactly-constant negative centered magnitude m, in the exact integer system (multiplicative denominator update plus the shape equation) with a n >= 2. It says nothing about variable, eventually-variable or cofinally-bounded negative magnitudes, which is where the live #243 obstruction sits, and the reciprocal series sum 1/a n is never formed in Lean in this zone, so no irrationality statement is touched.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Divisor propagation in the product-cleared orbit: every multiplier a(j) divides every strictly later denominator state D(k) for j < k; if a prime p divides both the current denominator state and the current multiplier then the shape equation D + e = (a-1) C together with C(n+1) = C(n) + e(n) forces p into the next tail state; and once p divides D(N) and C(N) it divides D(n), C(n) and e(n) at every later index n >= N.
statement_nodes.engine: divisibility transitivity along the multiplicative denominator update, plus the shape equation to carry the divisor into the tail state
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary divisibility bookkeeping in the exact integer system. It is the supply side of the divisor-lock pigeonhole used by the periodic no-go and of the coprimality bookkeeping used by the reduced-tail avoidance argument.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Statements about the exact integer recurrence system only (multiplicative denominator update, additive tail update, shape equation). Nothing here produces a divisor to lock, exhibits any concrete orbit, or touches the reciprocal series sum 1/a(n), which is never formed anywhere in this zone.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: There is no orbit with a(n) >= 2, a positive negative-magnitude sequence e that is periodic with period h and satisfies e(n) < a(n) pointwise, together with a fixed positive drift M of the tail state over one period and the exact shape equation D(n) + e(n) = (a(n) - 1) C(n); the eventual version holds too.
statement_nodes.engine: divisor lock plus phase-drift pigeonhole, with strong induction on M to remove a common scale
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The pointwise restriction e(n) < a(n) is an additional regime assumption (called the natural tail regime in the source), so this does not subsume the constant-negative theorem.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Closes only the exactly-periodic branch inside the natural tail regime. The Lean requires helt : forall n, e n < a n (a multiplier never divides its own phase magnitude), hepos : forall n, 0 < e n, exact periodicity e (n + h) = e n and a constant phase drift C (n + h) = C n + M with 0 < M. It therefore does not exclude aperiodic negative magnitudes, magnitudes with e n >= a n, magnitudes that are only approximately periodic, or the cofinally-bounded-negative branch that n243_no_cofinally_bounded_negative still leaves conditional. Because of helt it does not subsume n243_constant_negative_excluded. The reciprocal series itself is never formed anywhere in this zone.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Given finitely many pairwise-coprime moduli each greater than one, there are consecutive integers x, x+1, ..., x+k-1 with the i-th divisible by the i-th modulus, and the block can be pushed beyond any prescribed bound.
statement_nodes.engine: Chinese remainder theorem over a Finset plus a shift by a multiple of the modulus product
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard CRT / Chinese-remainder block construction; the Lean proof uses Mathlib's Nat.chineseRemainderOfFinset.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Along a reduced exact tail (coprime numerator and denominator at every index, with u(n+1) + v(n) = a(n) u(n) and v(n+1) = a(n) v(n)), the multipliers at distinct indices are pairwise coprime and every earlier multiplier is coprime to every later numerator.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary gcd bookkeeping; it is the supply side of the CRT barrier rather than a result about the reciprocal series.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A sequence of naturals tending to infinity cannot have uniformly bounded upward increments while permanently avoiding infinitely many fresh pairwise-coprime moduli; in particular no reduced exact tail whose numerator tends to infinity can have a uniformly bounded rise, in the strict or the eventual form.
statement_nodes.engine: shifted CRT forbidden window plus first-crossing of the block
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out only the bounded-rise regime for a reduced tail that is already known to tend to infinity. It does not rule out unbounded upward increments, tails that do not tend to infinity, orbits whose reduction fails to be coprime at every index, or any behaviour of the actual reciprocal series (which is never formed). It also says nothing once the gcd fails to stabilise, since the reduction step needs a fixed common divisor.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The tail gcd gcd(C(n), D(n)) divides its successor along an exact orbit, and at a negative-state index it equals gcd(C(n), e(n)), the gcd with the positive negative-state magnitude.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Two-line divisibility arguments; they make the tail gcd a divisibility chain so the 2^r budget applies.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If the exact orbit has cofinally many indices carrying a positive negative-state magnitude bounded by B, then the tail gcd is eventually constant. (The general ingredient is that a positive divisibility chain with cofinally bounded values is eventually constant.)
open_antecedents: hnegative : forall n, exists t e, n <= t and 0 < e and e <= B and D t + e = (a t - 1) * C t  (cofinally many uniformly bounded negative-state magnitudes; nothing in the corpus produces such indices for any actual reciprocal tail)

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: An exact orbit whose tail state tends to infinity, whose one-step rise is bounded by B, and which has cofinally many negative-state magnitudes in (0, B], is contradictory; the divergence of the tail state may itself be supplied by division-free normalized vanishing of a positive magnitude sequence.
open_antecedents: hRise : forall n, C (n + 1) <= C n + B  (uniformly bounded upward tail rise)
hnegative : forall n, exists t e, n <= t and 0 < e and e <= B and D t + e = (a t - 1) * C t  (cofinally bounded negative excursions)
hCTop : Filter.Tendsto C Filter.atTop Filter.atTop, or in the second form hvanish : forall K, exists N, forall n >= N, K * magnitude n < C n
statement_nodes.engine: gcd stabilisation followed by the reduced-tail CRT bounded-rise barrier

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Exact defect identity: (a' - (a^2 - a + 1)) * (a C - D) = a^2 (D - (a-1) C) - (D' - (a'-1) C') for the one-step images D' = a D, C' = a C - D. In words, the Sylvester defect times the next tail state equals a^2 times the current centered error minus the next centered error.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A polynomial identity closed by ring; it is the engine of the module but carries no independent mathematical content.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If two consecutive centered errors vanish and the next tail state is nonzero, then the multiplier takes the exact Sylvester step a' = a^2 - a + 1; along an exact orbit, eventual vanishing of the centered error together with eventual nonvanishing of the tail state gives the Sylvester recurrence from some index onward.
statement_nodes.engine: defect identity with a nonzero cofactor
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: This is the conversion that would turn eventual vanishing of E into the #243 conclusion; it is unconditional, but the eventual vanishing it consumes is not proved unconditionally anywhere in the zone.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Unconditional as a conversion, but both of its inputs are supplied nowhere unconditionally: eventual vanishing of the centered state is only produced by n243_boundednegative_rigidity, which carries three unproved hypotheses (normalized vanishing, bounded negative part, strict centering), and eventual nonvanishing of the tail state is an outright assumption. Nothing in the zone therefore derives the Sylvester recurrence for any actual orbit, and the reciprocal series is never formed.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If naturals satisfy C(n+1) + E(n) = C(n), then C is nonincreasing, hence eventually constant, and the nonnegative errors E vanish from some index onward.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Well-ordering of the naturals; the nonnegative branch of the wrapper.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The natural product-cleared recurrences realise the integer state maps: casting the natural tail and denominator recurrences gives exactly nextTailState and nextDenState, and hence the signed identity C(n+1) = C(n) - E(n) over the integers.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Cast bookkeeping between the natural and integer presentations of the same system.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: In the strict-centering regime |E(n)| < C(n) for all n, a vanishing centered error is absorbing: E(n) = 0 forces E(n+1) = 0, because the defect identity makes C(n+1) divide E(n+1) and the only multiple of smaller absolute value is zero. Failure of eventual vanishing therefore makes every error on the tail nonzero.
statement_nodes.engine: defect identity plus the divisor-versus-absolute-value argument
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The hypothesis |E(n)| < C(n) is a centering normalisation of the representative rather than an open input, so this is recorded as unconditional; it is nonetheless never verified for any concrete orbit in the zone.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The strict-centering hypothesis hcentered : forall n, Int.natAbs (E n) < C n is a free hypothesis of centeredState_zero_absorbing that is discharged nowhere in the corpus, and the very same hypothesis is listed as an open antecedent of n243_boundednegative_rigidity. It is recorded here as a regime normalisation (for an exact orbit the multiplier a n can be chosen so that E is a centred representative) rather than as an open input, but that choice is the only reason this node is not a conditional_implication. The theorem therefore says nothing about orbits outside the strictly centred regime, and no concrete orbit is exhibited inside it. eventually_nonzero_of_zero_absorbing is pure logic on an abstract E and carries no arithmetic at all.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Headline of the #243 module: for an exact natural orbit with a(n) > 1, positive tail state, strict centering |E(n)| < C(n), a uniform lower bound -B <= E(n), and division-free normalized vanishing of E relative to C, the centered error vanishes from some index onward. An eventual form allows the centering and the lower bound to start at different indices.
open_antecedents: hvanish : forall K, exists N, forall n, N <= n -> K * Int.natAbs (E n) < C n  (division-free normalized vanishing; the dominant unproved input)
hbound : forall n, -(B : Int) <= E n  (bounded negative part of the centered error)
hcentered : forall n, Int.natAbs (E n) < C n  (strict centering of the representative)
statement_nodes.engine: case split on cofinal negativity: CRT bounded-rise barrier on one branch, monotone stabilisation on the other
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Combined with n243_sylvester_from_vanishing this would give the eventual Sylvester recurrence, i.e. the #243 rigidity conclusion, but only under the three hypotheses above and only for an orbit that is never derived from a rational value of the reciprocal series.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Survival through h forced divisions of the map a -> ((n+1)a^2 - (n+2)a + (n+3))/(n+2) depends only on the initial state modulo the ascending-factorial horizon modulus, which at the initial index equals (h+1)!.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Polynomial compatibility with congruences plus exact division; the only work is tracking the divided-out factor. The module itself states it is finite-horizon only.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: forcedSurvives_iff_of_modEq_factorial converts the question 'does this state survive h forced divisions' into the question 'does its class mod (h+1)! survive', i.e. it makes a fixed finite horizon decidable. It is not a statement about the actual #243 objects: the module docstring states explicitly that the result is finite-horizon only and 'neither constructs an infinite negative-state orbit nor rules one out'. Survivors do exist at every finite horizon; only the infinite orbit is excluded, and that exclusion comes from n243_constant_negative_excluded, not from here.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The first two zero-based consecutive prime gaps are 1 and 2 (3 - 2 and 5 - 3).
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Two simp evaluations of Nat.nth Nat.Prime at 0, 1, 2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The displayed zero-based partial sum of p(i)/2^i equals twice the partial sum in the convention with denominator 2^(i+1).
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Index convention bookkeeping only.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Exact finite summation by parts for dyadic partial sums: the sum of P(i)/2^(i+1) over i < n+1 equals P(0) plus the dyadic sum of forward differences minus the endpoint term P(n)/2^(n+1); specialised to the primes this rewrites the dyadic prime partial sum as 2 plus the dyadic prime-gap partial sum minus an endpoint correction.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Finite Abel summation. The endpoint term is retained, so passing to the infinite series still needs a separate convergence argument, as the source docstring states.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For any rational sequence obeying the dyadic tail recurrence T(N+1) = 2 T(N) - g(N+1) with integer digits, iterating h steps gives T(N+h) = 2^h T(N) - B(h,N) with B the explicit integer block, so the shifted difference T(N+h) - T(N) equals (2^h - 1) T(N) minus that integer block; the shift also propagates one step at a time.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exact unrolling of a linear recurrence; the recurrence is a hypothesis on an abstract pair and is never instantiated at the prime-gap series in this zone.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: A shifted tail difference is an integer exactly when (2^h - 1) times the current tail state is an integer, because the two differ by an explicit integer block.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Both sides are concrete conditions on a rational number; neither side is open.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a rational has odd reduced denominator d then (2^phi(d) - 1) times it is an integer; consequently a tail state with odd reduced denominator has an integral shift after phi(d) steps.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Euler's congruence 2^phi(d) = 1 mod d for odd d; formalised through Mathlib's Nat.ModEq.pow_totient.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Once a fixed tail shift is integral at one index it is integral at every later index, by the recurrence alone and with no prime-distribution input.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Immediate induction on the recurrence; about the abstract class of integer-digit dyadic recurrences, not about prime gaps.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: An arbitrary integer carry sequence K emits the dyadic coefficients 2K(n) - K(n+1) whose partial sums telescope exactly to K(0) - K(n)/2^n. Hence a rational dyadic value is compatible with a completely unconstrained, in particular non-periodic, coefficient stream; rationality alone cannot force eventual periodicity or automaticity of the coefficient word.
statement_nodes.engine: exact telescoping of the dyadic coboundary
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The Lean content is weaker than the barrier reading. carryPartialSum_eq is a finite telescoping identity (carryPartialSum K n = K 0 - K n / 2^n) and natCarryCoeff_cast is a cast lemma; no limit is taken in Lean, no series is shown to converge, no aperiodic carry sequence with a rational dyadic value is instantiated, and no Lean statement has the form 'X cannot work'. The no-go is an editorial reading of the identity, one unformalised limit step away from being formal. Within that reading it rules out only the inference 'rational dyadic value implies eventually periodic or automatic coefficient stream' via the coboundary identity alone. It does not rule out irrationality of the dyadic prime or prime-gap series, does not use or contradict any size or growth property of the actual prime gaps, and does not rule out arguments based on growing-block dyadic anti-concentration, which the module names as the missing producer. The natural-valued version needs K (n+1) <= 2 K n, so nonnegativity of the emitted coefficients is a real constraint that the barrier does not remove.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For three pairwise-distinct primes p, q, r and x nonzero, the least common multiple of all {p,q,r}-smooth numbers not exceeding x equals the product of the largest pure powers p^log_p x * q^log_q x * r^log_r x.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary: each pure power occurs in the prefix and prime powers of distinct primes are coprime.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The three-prime height, the literal smooth-prefix LCM and the reciprocal lattice kernel are all constant on a logarithmic cell, i.e. whenever none of the three floor-logarithm coordinates changes.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Immediate from the definition of the height once the LCM identity is available.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For three pairwise-distinct primes, the first count positive powers in each channel are distinct and pairwise disjoint across channels, giving 3*count values; adjoining the common origin 1 gives exactly 3*count + 1 distinct jump values.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Unique factorisation; a counting statement about the jump ladder, not about any series value.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If exactly one floor-logarithm coordinate advances by one, the three-prime height, and hence the running LCM, is multiplied by exactly the corresponding prime base.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: One-line consequence of the product form of the height.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Grouping the finite smooth exponent box by running-LCM height puts the finite kernel sum in normal form: the coefficient of each height is the cardinality of its fiber times the reciprocal of that height.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Finset fiberwise regrouping of a finite sum; no analytic content.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For any bases and any nonzero x, the three-prime height is at most x^3, since each pure-power component is at most x.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Three applications of Nat.pow_log_le_self.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The first exact {2,3,5} kernel values: 1 at the origin, 1/2 at exponent (1,0,0), 1/6 at (0,1,0) and 1/60 at (1,1,0).
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Four norm_num evaluations of floor logarithms at 1, 2, 3, 6.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The {2,3,5} kernel is not of rank one: the product of the values at (0,0,0) and (1,1,0) is 1/60 while the product at (1,0,0) and (0,1,0) is 1/12, so the kernel does not factor as a product of one-dimensional channels.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The smallest explicit obstruction to a separable (rank-one) treatment of the three-prime kernel; verified at four lattice points only.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The variable-base tail step next = base * (state - digit) is the same as next = base * state - base * digit.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A distributivity restatement; the tail orbit it names is not connected to any series in this zone.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: In a half-open multiplicative interval of width at most one base, fixing the other exponents pins that base's exponent; hence a {p,q,r}-smooth exponent shell in such an interval injects into a two-coordinate box, and when the coordinate heights are sorted and sum to j the shell cardinality obeys 9 * card <= (j + 3)^2.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Standard short-interval smooth-number counting: within a window of multiplicative width at most the base, one exponent is determined; the (j+3)^2/9 form is the AM-GM bound on (a+1)(b+1).

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a positive natural c is at most bound and is congruent modulo C to a residue lying strictly above bound and at most C, that is contradictory; equivalently, a bounded positive state in the window forces its prescribed residue to stay within the bound.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Two omega-level facts about least positive residues. The module itself disclaims the open producer: nothing here asserts that an escaping block exists for every putative rational denominator, which is the entire content of the residue-escape strategy.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Two exact arithmetic facts supporting the published 7/2 lane: 2^18 < 7^7, and 7/18 = 1/2 - 1/9 as rationals.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The irrationality at base 7/2 is Bundschuh-Vaananen's published theorem; these two norm_num facts are only the arithmetic scraps of its margin computation, and the logarithmic monotonicity step and the estimate 3 < pi are deliberately left outside.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These are two norm_num facts (2^18 < 7^7 and 7/18 = 1/2 - 1/9). They do not formalise Bundschuh-Vaananen, do not establish log 2 / log 7 < 7/18 (the logarithmic monotonicity step is deliberately outside the module), do not supply 3 < pi, and do not establish irrationality of the Lambert value at base 7/2 or at any other base. No irrationality statement about 7/2 exists in Lean anywhere in this corpus.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The coordinatewise rational-base corridor for natural parameters (a,b,N,K,Q,digit) is exactly the conjunction a > 0, Q > 0, digit > 0, digit <= N+K, a^K divides Q*digit, and Q*b^(N+K+1) < a^(K+1). It packages the simultaneous coordinate-clearing divisibility and subunit tail estimate used in the elementary rational-base obstruction.
statement_nodes.engine: A six-parameter predicate retaining exactly the positivity, coefficient-size, divisibility, and tail-smallness conditions of the coordinatewise clearing scheme.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An exact packaging of the elementary coordinatewise clearing conditions used in the manuscript; no novelty claim is made for the definition.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This is a predicate, not an existence theorem. It neither supplies a corridor nor asserts anything about the Lambert series value; the separate no-go theorem excludes only this literal corridor shape at base 3/2.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If a coordinatewise rational-base corridor holds with numerator base a and denominator base b, i.e. a^K divides Q*digit with 0 < digit <= N+K and Q b^(N+K+1) < a^(K+1), then b^(N+K+1) < a (N+K): the corridor converts into a power-versus-linear inequality.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Elementary divisibility plus cancellation; it is the transport used by the 3/2 no-go.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: At base 3/2 no coordinatewise corridor can occur once both the shift N and the cleared window K are at least one, because exponential growth 2^(N+K+1) already beats 3(N+K).
statement_nodes.engine: power-versus-linear transport plus induction on 3x < 2^(x+1)
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Rules out only the literal coordinatewise transfer of the integer-base Erdos corridor at the single base 3/2, and only when N >= 1 and K >= 1. statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For rational r,s, an abstract coefficient sequence c and cutoff N, the rational-base prefix is P_N = sum over 0 <= m < N of c(m+1)*s^(m+1)/r^(m+1). Given rational B and a putative value F, the corresponding cleared-tail coordinate is U_N = B*r^N*(F-P_N).
statement_nodes.engine: Exact finite-sum and denominator-cleared state coordinates over the rationals.

statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These are definitions for an arbitrary rational F and abstract coefficients. They do not identify F with an infinite Lambert series, prove convergence, make U_N integral or bounded, or establish irrationality.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Exact rational-base cleared-tail recurrence: with prefix sum of coeff(m+1) s^(m+1)/r^(m+1) and cleared tail B r^N (F - prefix), one has cleared(N+1) = r * cleared(N) - B coeff(N+1) s^(N+1). The forcing term carries the factor s^(N+1), which is the denominator-base tax absent from the integer-base case s = 1.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Field_simp/ring identity over the rationals; F is an arbitrary rational, so nothing is asserted about the actual Lambert value.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For natural denominator base s, clearing multiplier B, coefficient sequence c and cutoff N, the natural forcing magnitude is exactly G_N = B*c(N+1)*s^(N+1), the inhomogeneous term whose size is compared across integer and noninteger denominator bases.
statement_nodes.engine: A natural-valued coordinate isolating the absolute magnitude B*c(N+1)*s^(N+1) of the cleared recurrence's forcing term.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A direct coordinate definition extracted from the cleared-tail recurrence.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The definition imposes no positivity assumptions and proves no growth by itself. Its exponential lower bound for s >= 2 and collapse at s = 1 are separate theorems.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For denominator base s >= 2, positive B and positive coefficients, the natural-valued forcing magnitude B * coeff(N+1) * s^(N+1) is at least 2^(N+1); in the integer-base case s = 1 it collapses to B * coeff(N+1).
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A one-line monotonicity of powers. It quantifies the denominator-base tax but proves nothing about convergence, positivity or irrationality.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: A monotonicity of powers under s >= 2, 1 <= B, 1 <= coeff (N+1). It quantifies the denominator-base tax and nothing else: no convergence, no positivity of any remainder, and no irrationality follows, and the coefficients are abstract rather than the actual divisor function.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: The doubled rational-Pade denominator coordinates are defined over the integers by E~(n) = 3n^2-n for the proposed common exponent, P~(n,k) = 2(k(n-k)+nk)+k(k-1) for a homogenised P summand, and, with j=n-m-1, Q~(n,m) = 2(n^2-n)+j^2+2jm+j-m^2+3m for the maximal Q-summand exponent.
statement_nodes.engine: Three exact integer-valued polynomial coordinates with exponents doubled to remove floors and parity bookkeeping.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: The displayed exponent expressions are formalised exactly as manuscript coordinates. The manuscript explicitly does not derive them from a homogenised coefficient formula or claim a new Pade construction.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: These definitions contain only exponent bookkeeping. They do not prove coefficient integrality, derive the expressions from a Pade construction, establish nonvanishing or positivity of a remainder, control its decay, or imply irrationality.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: Doubled denominator-exponent bookkeeping for the rational Pade homogenisation: for 0 <= k <= n the doubled P-summand exponent 2(k(n-k) + nk) + k(k-1) never exceeds 3n^2 - n, the gap factoring as (n-k)(3n-k-1); the doubled Q-maximum satisfies the exact gap identity 3n^2 - n - Qmax = 2(n + m(m-1)), hence is also bounded by 3n^2 - n whenever m >= 1.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Polynomial inequalities closed by nlinarith. The Pade / little-q-Legendre construction they serve is classical (Bundschuh-Vaananen, Van Assche); the module states that positivity of the Pade remainder and its asymptotics remain separate unproved analytic obligations, so no irrationality content is present.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Denominator-exponent bookkeeping only, over Z with every exponent doubled to avoid floors and parity. The module states that positivity of the Pade remainder and its asymptotics remain separate analytic obligations; neither is formalised here or elsewhere in the corpus, so no Pade irrationality argument is closed by these inequalities. The Q-bound additionally needs m >= 1, so the m = 0 summand is not covered.
